analysis.investment_thesis: City Union Bank is a conservatively run regional bank with a 120-year track record, consistent earnings growth of ~14% CAGR, and a forward P/E of just 12.5x — making the PEG the most reasonable in this group at roughly 1.1x. It's not a ten-bagger story, but it's an honest stalwart at a fair price.
key_strengths: Net profit has compounded at 13.9% over 3 years (INR 760 Cr → INR 1,124 Cr) with no year of decline — rare consistency for a regional bank
Forward P/E of 12.54x with PEG near 1.0 — the most GARP-friendly valuation metric I can find across this cohort
Borrowings cut nearly in half from INR 5,312 Cr to INR 1,790 Cr (FY22→FY25), indicating disciplined liability management and balance sheet strengthening
key_risks: Revenue CAGR of only 6.3% — slow-grower pace that limits the size of the opportunity; this won't double revenue in 5 years
Finance costs growing at 17.2% CAGR (much faster than 6.3% revenue growth) signals NIM compression risk as deposit costs remain elevated
ROE of 11.87% sits just below my 12% threshold — a mediocre return on equity for shareholders, meaning capital efficiency needs to improve
red_flags: Operating cash flow collapsed from INR 1,166 Cr (FY22) to INR 436 Cr (FY24) before recovering to INR 1,128 Cr in FY25 — the volatility makes trend analysis unreliable for a bank
P/B of 1.92x is acceptable but leaves no margin of safety if asset quality deteriorates — single-state concentration in Tamil Nadu amplifies regional economic risk
Revenue in FY24 actually contracted from FY23 (INR 2,973 Cr → INR 2,865 Cr) — a top-line shrinkage year is not what I want to see mid-cycle
analysis.detailed_analysis:
City Union Bank is the kind of quiet, conservative franchise that's been running its business for over a century without blowing up. It doesn't have the flashiest growth profile, but it competes well in SME and trader financing in South India — a niche I respect. The steady profit climb from INR 760 Cr to INR 1,124 Cr over three years is reassuring, and the balance sheet cleanup (debt nearly halved) shows management is thinking long-term.

Banks are inherently complex animals — leverage, credit cycles, and regulation make them harder to evaluate simply. At forward P/E of 12.5x and PEG around 1.1x, you're not overpaying, but you're not getting a bargain either. The revenue slowdown, rising funding costs, and sub-12% ROE mean this is a HOLD, not a BUY. I'd need to see ROE sustainably above 14% and revenue growth re-accelerating past 10% to get excited.
